| `quarantine/` | Sessions that were too large or unreadable |
| `capture-state.gen/` | Which sessions Capture has already seen. `capture-state.json` next to it is a copy for reading: editing it changes nothing |
| `.internal/` | The Codex model Capture picked for each level |
| `embeddings/` | A cache of embeddings, when Search by meaning is on |
| `briefs/`, `project-index.json` | Prepared project briefs and the map from sessions to projects |
| `observability/` | Local logs: capture runs, index and embedding events, which MCP tools were called, the update check |
| `rift.pid` | The engine's process ID while it runs |

## The database

Onadit uses [LanceDB](https://lancedb.com), an embedded database. Nothing listens on the network for it.

| Table | Holds | Main columns |
|---|---|---|
| `conversations_hot` | Current conversations. Every save and import lands here | `id`, `content`, `summary`, `embedding`, `source`, `domain`, `intent`, `quality`, `topics`, `decisions`, `key_outputs`, `indexed_at`, `idempotency_key` |
| `conversations_cold` | Archived conversations older than 30 days. Filled only when you run `onadit compact`, which needs Search by meaning and Codex or local enrichment. Nothing runs it on its own | Same as above |
| `digests` | Summaries written by `onadit compact` | `id`, `content`, `summary`, `embedding`, `period_start`, `period_end`, `digest_type` |
| `structured_docs` | Documents from folders you asked Onadit to index | `id`, `source_path`, `content`, `embedding`, `source_type`, `source_scope`, `indexed_at` |
| `structured_docs_local` | The same, for sources embedded on your Mac | Same as above |

Embeddings have 512 dimensions, or 768 for sources embedded on your Mac. A conversation imported with Search by meaning off is stored with an empty vector and found by keyword. When you turn Search by meaning on in Onadit.app, the whole archive is embedded once.

## Outside the Onadit folder

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `~/Applications/Onadit.app` | The app |
| `~/.rift/bin/onadit` | The command line, on a package install. `~/.rift/bin/rift` is the same command under its earlier name |
| npm's global folder | The `onadit` package, on a terminal install |
| `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.getrift.daemon.plist` | The launch agent |
| `~/Library/Logs/Rift/` | Engine logs, on a package install |
| `~/Library/Application Support/SwiftBar/Plugins/rift.10s.sh` | The menu-bar plugin, with its helper in `.rift-menu/` next to it |
| `~/.rift.env` | Your Voyage key, if you saved one. Readable by you only. |
| macOS Keychain, service `com.getrift.daemon` | The tokens the command line and the app use to talk to the engine |
| `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` | An `onadit` entry, if you connected Claude |
| `~/.claude.json` | An `onadit` entry, if you connected Claude Code |
| `~/.codex/config.toml` | An `onadit` entry, if you connected Codex |
| `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | An `onadit` entry, if you connected Cursor |
| `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.claude/hooks/rift-policy.mjs` | Onadit's hooks, if you turned them on for Claude Code |
| `~/.codex/hooks.json` | Onadit's hooks, if you turned them on for Codex |

## Folders Onadit reads and never changes

| Folder | Read by |
|---|---|
| `~/.claude/projects/` | Capture, for Claude Code sessions |
| `~/.codex/sessions/` and `~/.codex/archived_sessions/` | Capture, for Codex sessions |
| `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/` | Capture, only if you opt in to Cowork sessions |
| `~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb` | Capture, only if you add Cursor to `capture.sources` |
| `~/.grok/` | Capture, only if you opt in to Grok CLI sessions |

## Back up or move the archive

The archive is ordinary files in `~/Library/Application Support/Rift/data/`. To keep it somewhere else, stop the engine, move everything in `data/` except `config.json` to the new place, set `data_paths.data_dir` in `config.json` to that folder's absolute path, then start the engine. `config.json` itself stays where it is. Onadit does not move the files for you: without them, the engine starts on an empty archive.

```sh
launchctl bootout gui/$UID/com.getrift.daemon
# move the files and edit config.json, then:
launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.getrift.daemon.plist
```


---
title: Privacy, in plain words
url: https://onadit.com/docs/privacy
summary: Onadit stores your conversations and search index on your Mac. Conversation content leaves only through the choices described on this page.
last_updated: 2026-10-22
---

# Privacy, in plain words

Onadit stores your conversations and search index on your Mac. Conversation content leaves only through the choices described on this page.

## The short version

A fresh install uses keyword search and makes no AI calls. No Onadit account is needed. Your conversation content leaves only through the choices described below. There is also a version check, which sends no content.

Search by meaning sends text to Voyage's models, with a key Onadit gives you or with your own. AI processing uses your own accounts. 2 things can reach me: a random install ID if you ask Onadit for a search key, and feedback if you enable the relay. When you ask your AI tool to search Onadit, the excerpts it retrieves become part of that tool's chat.

Every network call is listed, one by one, in [What leaves your Mac](https://onadit.com/docs/egress.md).

## Search by meaning, off until you turn it on

Turn it on and search gets smarter. From then on, the text Onadit indexes and the queries you type are sent out to be embedded by Voyage's models. Turned on in the app, it also sends everything already in your archive, once, so all of it can be searched by meaning. There are 2 ways to turn it on.

In the app, Onadit asks my key service for a key. That request carries a random install ID and, like any web request, your IP address, which is used to limit how many keys 1 address can get. It carries no content, no name and no email. The key is for Voyage's models as hosted by MongoDB Atlas, and I pay for it. Your text then goes from your Mac to that service directly, not through me.

Or add your own Voyage API key, and your text goes to `api.voyageai.com` under your account, with nothing sent to me. With search by meaning off, nothing is embedded and nothing is sent.

## AI enrichment and capture, only if you opt in

These features are off by default. When enabled, metadata extraction and capture triage send conversation content to your configured worker: Codex CLI (OpenAI) or Claude Code (Anthropic), under your own account. Capture also sends a short test message before each run, and with Codex as the worker, a session too large to judge is later sent whole, in pieces, to be summarised. Digest summaries use Codex. Choosing Claude for metadata does not silently enable Codex digests. A local Ollama model can do metadata and digest work on your Mac instead.

## When your AI tool uses Onadit

When Claude, Codex, Cursor, or another connected tool calls Onadit, matching conversation excerpts and their source references enter that chat. A cloud AI tool can send this context to its provider under your account and its own privacy settings. If you turn on the optional session hooks, a short project note also enters every new Claude Code or Codex session this way. The local browser search stays on your Mac unless you have enabled cloud search.

## Feedback, off by default

Your `onadit feedback` notes are saved locally. A note only reaches me if you turned on the feedback relay, during `onadit onboard` or with `onadit feedback setup`, and then just your note and its tag, a random per-install ID (not your name or hostname), your email if you chose to share one, the Onadit, commit and Node versions, and optional health information such as whether the daemon is running. The relay runs on Cloudflare and emails each note to me through Resend. Leave the relay off and nothing is sent.

## A version check

About once an hour the app pings `registry.npmjs.org` to see if a newer version exists, the same plain request `npm install` makes. No content, no ID, no key.

## What never happens

No telemetry to me. No usage counters, no crash reports, no analytics, no snippets or embeddings phoned home. The Onadit app never sends your conversations or search activity to me. The only things it sends me are a feedback note you opt into and type yourself, and the random install ID when you ask Onadit for a search key.

## The email form on this site

Separate from the app: if you leave your email on this site, it is stored in my contact list at Resend, an email provider, so I can write to you about Onadit. The email is all it collects, and skipping the form stores nothing. It has nothing to do with the app, which never uploads your conversations or search activity.

## Visit counts on this site

Also separate from the app: this website counts visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics. It sees which pages are viewed, the site you came from, your browser, device type and country, and how fast pages load. It sets no cookies and does not follow you to other sites.

## Leaving is 1 command

In the macOS setup page, choose Remove Onadit and confirm once. This removes Onadit's archive, credentials, background service, bundled app and its connections to your AI tools. Original exports and unrelated tools are preserved.

The same removal is available from Terminal with `onadit uninstall --purge-data`. Without `--purge-data`, your archive and credentials are kept. A setup-page removal leaves a report in `~/Library/Logs/Rift/` and tells you if any step failed. Separately installed npm packages need their package manager's uninstall command. Each step is described in [Remove Onadit](https://onadit.com/docs/remove.md).

## This page is the contract

If the app ever does something this page does not say, that is a bug. Run `onadit feedback --kind=broke` and I will fix it.


---
title: What leaves your Mac
url: https://onadit.com/docs/egress
summary: A list of every network call Onadit can make, what it sends, and whether it is on. Out of the box, only an update check leaves your Mac.
last_updated: 2026-10-22
---

# What leaves your Mac

A list of every network call Onadit can make, what it sends, and whether it is on. Out of the box, only an update check leaves your Mac.

## The short version

- Your archive is stored on your Mac, with no account and no cloud copy, and we never receive your conversations
- Keyword search, import and the MCP server work with nothing sent anywhere
- Text leaves your Mac only through features you turn on: Search by meaning, Capture, AI enrichment, a feedback note you send, and an agent recalling a passage

## Every call

| Call | Goes to | Sends | On by default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Update check | `registry.npmjs.org` | A plain request for the package's version list. Nothing about you | Yes. At start, then hourly. There is no switch to turn it off |
| Embeddings | Voyage's models: `api.voyageai.com` with your own key, or `ai.mongodb.com` (MongoDB Atlas, which hosts them) with a key from Onadit | The text to embed: search questions, saved and imported conversations, indexed documents. Turned on in the app, also your whole existing archive, once. See below | No. Needs Search by meaning |
| Key check | The same embedding service | The fixed text `rift onboarding probe` | Only when a key is added |
| Key service | Our key service, `rift-relay.clem-rog.workers.dev`, which runs on Cloudflare | A random install ID. No text, no email. Like any web request, it shows your IP address, which we use to limit how many keys 1 address can get | No. Only when you turn Search by meaning on in the app |
| Capture check | Your own Claude Code or Codex, with your sign-in | A fixed test message, before each Capture run | No. Needs Capture |
| Codex model check | Your own Codex | Up to 4 tiny test calls when Codex lists a model Onadit has not tried, to find one that runs | No. Needs Codex for Capture or enrichment |
| Session judging | Your own Claude Code or Codex | The session transcript, cut to about 256 KB, and a prompt. With Codex as the worker, a session over 8 MB is later sent whole, in 512 KB pieces, to be summarised | No. Needs Capture |
| Richer summaries and digests | Your own Claude Code or Codex | Conversation text | No. Needs enrichment |
| Commands you run | Your own Codex | The text they work on. `onadit triage --dir`, `onadit backfill --provider codex-cli` and `onadit capture recover-quarantine` use Codex whatever your settings | Only when you run them |
| Feedback | Our feedback relay, which runs on Cloudflare and emails each note to us through Resend | The note and its tag, the time, a random install ID, your email if you shared one, the Onadit, commit and Node versions, and a status snapshot if you add `--with-status` | No. Only if you turn the relay on, with an invite |
| Sign-up | The same relay | Your email and install ID, once | Only if you give an email when you turn the relay on |

The engine itself listens on `127.0.0.1` only. It cannot be reached from the network.

## Search by meaning

When it is on, Onadit sends text to Voyage to turn it into embeddings: every question an agent or you search for, and every conversation or document that enters the archive. The embeddings come back and are stored on your Mac.

If you turn it on in Onadit.app, Onadit also sends everything already in your archive, once: current and archived conversations, digests and documents, so all of it can be searched by meaning. Adding your own key with `onadit onboard --voyage-key` does not send what is already there. `onadit reindex` would.

There are 2 ways to turn it on.

| How | The key | Where your text goes |
|---|---|---|
| In Onadit.app, under Privacy | Onadit asks our key service for one, sending a random install ID. It is for Voyage's models as hosted by MongoDB Atlas, we pay for it, and it is saved in `~/.rift.env` | From your Mac to `ai.mongodb.com` directly, not through us |
| `onadit onboard --voyage-key <key>` | Your own Voyage key | To `api.voyageai.com`, under your account. Nothing is sent to us |

With it off, search is by keyword and nothing is sent.

## Capture

Capture needs Search by meaning, so everything above applies. It also runs your own Claude Code or Codex on each new session, which sends that session's text to Anthropic or OpenAI under your account. A short test message goes the same way before each run. See [Capture](https://onadit.com/docs/capture.md#what-your-tool-is-asked-to-do) for the commands.

Onadit holds no Anthropic or OpenAI key and makes no call to either on its own.

## When an agent recalls a passage

This is the one that is easy to miss. When a connected agent calls an Onadit tool, the passages it gets back become part of its conversation. They go wherever the rest of that conversation goes: to the agent's provider.

The optional session hooks for Claude Code and Codex go further: they put a project note of about 2 KB into every new session, with no tool call. It holds lines from your tracker files and summaries of the project's latest captured sessions, and it reaches the provider the same way.

Onadit decides what to return. It cannot decide what the agent does with it.

The archive is 1 pool. Passing `cwd` narrows documents and puts the current project's conversations first in a context pack. It does not keep the rest out: a passage from another project can still be returned, and `onadit_search` does not filter conversations by `cwd`. If you work under terms that keep one client's material away from another's tools, take that into account before you connect an agent.

## What we can see

| | |
|---|---|
| Your conversations | Never |
| Your searches | Never |
| That an install exists | Only if you turn Search by meaning on in the app, or turn the feedback relay on: 1 random ID, and the IP address the request came from |
| Your email | Only if you give it to us |
| A feedback note | Only the notes you send through the relay |

## Check it yourself

- The table above lists every call the engine and the command line make, and on a terminal install `onadit update` also downloads the new version from npm when you run it
- The package also holds code for direct calls to `api.anthropic.com` and `api.openai.com` that this version never runs, so a search of its files finds those addresses
- The engine's log is in `~/Library/Logs/Rift/` on a package install, and in `~/Library/Application Support/Rift/logs/` on a terminal install
- `data/observability/embedding-events.jsonl` is a local record of embedding requests
- `data/observability/agent-tool-usage.jsonl` is a local record of the tool calls your agents made
- `onadit status` shows whether a key is loaded and whether Capture is on


---
title: Remove Onadit
url: https://onadit.com/docs/remove
summary: Removing Onadit from the app deletes your archive. Removing it from the command line keeps the archive unless you ask otherwise.
last_updated: 2026-10-22
---

# Remove Onadit

Removing Onadit from the app deletes your archive. Removing it from the command line keeps the archive unless you ask otherwise.

## From the app

Onadit.app and the setup page have a Remove Onadit action. It always deletes the archive. It runs the command below with `--purge-data`.

## From the command line

```sh
onadit uninstall               # stops Onadit, keeps your archive
onadit uninstall --purge-data  # also deletes the archive, after you type DELETE
```

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--purge-data` | Also deletes `~/Library/Application Support/Rift/`, then your saved key and tokens |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Skips the `DELETE` confirmation. Only with `--purge-data` |
| `--notify` | Writes a log to `~/Library/Logs/Rift/` and shows the result on screen |
| `--json` | Also prints the outcome as JSON, after the text lines |

The command exits with code 1 if any step failed, and lists what is left with the commands to remove it by hand.

## What happens, in order

1. The engine is stopped
2. The launch agent is backed up, then deleted
3. Onadit's entry is removed from Claude, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, each config file backed up first
4. Onadit's hooks are removed from Claude Code and Codex, each settings file backed up first, and `~/.claude/hooks/rift-policy.mjs` is deleted
5. With `--purge-data` only: `~/Library/Application Support/Rift/` is deleted
6. If that worked: `~/.rift.env` and Onadit's Keychain tokens are deleted
7. In every case: the command-line shim, the menu-bar plugin files and `~/Applications/Onadit.app` are deleted

## What is kept without --purge-data

- `~/Library/Application Support/Rift/`, which holds your archive, the job queue and the engine files
- `~/.rift.env`, if you saved a Voyage key (the command tells you how to delete it)
- Onadit's tokens in the Keychain

The `onadit` command itself is gone after this. To delete the archive later, remove the folder, `~/.rift.env` and the Keychain items by hand.

## What is never removed

These are left in place in every mode. Delete them by hand if you want a clean machine.

| Left behind | Where |
|---|---|
| Logs | `~/Library/Logs/Rift/` |
| Launch agent backups | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.getrift.daemon.plist.bak.*` |
| Backups of your MCP config and hook settings files | Next to each file, named `<file>.bak.*` |
| Terminal-install leftovers | `~/.local/bin/onadit`, the `PATH` block in `~/.zshrc`, and the global npm package |
| SwiftBar | Wherever you installed it |

> If you moved the data folder with `data_paths.data_dir`, `--purge-data` does not delete it. It only deletes the default folder.


---
title: Command line
url: https://onadit.com/docs/cli
summary: Every onadit command, with its options. On a package install the command lives at ~/.rift/bin/onadit.
last_updated: 2026-10-22
---

# Command line

Every onadit command, with its options. On a package install the command lives at ~/.rift/bin/onadit.

## Where the command is

A package install puts the command at `~/.rift/bin/onadit` and leaves your `PATH` alone. A terminal install puts it in npm's global folder and, if `onadit` is not already on your `PATH`, links `~/.local/bin/onadit` and adds that folder to your `PATH` in `~/.zshrc`. To type `onadit` on its own after a package install:

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/.rift/bin:$PATH"
```

`rift`, the command's name before Onadit was renamed, still works and runs the same command.

In the usage lines below, `<angle brackets>` mark a value you must give, and `[square brackets]` mark something optional. An option shown outside square brackets is required.

## Global options

These work with every command, with the exceptions noted for `--json`.

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--config <path>` | Use another `config.json`. Default: `~/Library/Application Support/Rift/data/config.json`, or `RIFT_CONFIG` if set |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON. Ignored by `onboard`, `setup`, `mcp install`, `hooks`, `feedback` and `token issue`, which print text. `uninstall` prints its text lines too, then the JSON |
| `-V`, `--version` | Print the version |
| `-h`, `--help` | Print help for the command |

## Everyday commands

### onadit status

Shows what the engine is doing, in about 12 lines, and 1 next action.

```sh
onadit status [--tools] [--no-capability-map] [--json]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--tools` | Also print the guide your agents see |
| `--no-capability-map` | With `--json`, leave that guide out. For scripts that poll often |

The lines are explained in [Troubleshooting](https://onadit.com/docs/troubleshooting.md#what-onadit-status-prints).

### onadit doctor

Checks the same things as `status`, names what is wrong in plain language, and gives 1 action. `onadit doctor` on its own only reads. It exits with code 1 when something is broken.

```sh
onadit doctor [--copy-prompt] [--target claude|codex]
onadit doctor repair capture-large-sessions [--dry-run] [--chunk-bytes <bytes>]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--copy-prompt` | Builds a repair prompt with private details removed, copies it, and prints it, so you can hand the problem to an agent |
| `--target <assistant>` | Which assistant the prompt is written for: `claude` (default) or `codex` |
| `repair capture-large-sessions` | Saves the Codex sessions that were too large for Capture. Codex summarises each one in pieces, and it is saved as 1 conversation. `--dry-run` shows what would be saved |

### onadit search

Searches the archive from the terminal. It is the same search your agents use.

```sh
onadit search "why did we drop the queue" --scope conversations --top-k 5
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--scope <scope>` | `all`, `clients`, `projects`, `conversations` or `documents` |
| `--client <name>` | Only files from 1 client's folder. Conversations are not filtered |
| `--since <time>` | Only results indexed on or after this UTC time, written in full, such as `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`. A date alone is refused |
| `--top-k <n>` | How many results |
| `--detail <level>` | `summary` (default), `middle` (the start and end of the text) or `full` |
| `--id <id>` | With `middle` or `full`, fetch 1 result by its ID |
| `--tier <tier>` | With `--id`: `hot`, `cold`, `digest`, `document` or `structured_doc` |
| `--source-table <name>` | With `--id`: the table the row lives in |

### onadit brief

Prints the project brief Onadit has prepared for a folder.

```sh
onadit brief [--cwd <dir>] [--hook]
```

`--hook` is for the SessionStart hook of Claude Code or Codex. It reads the hook payload on standard input.

### onadit setup

Opens Onadit.app to import chats and connect your tools. If the app is not installed, or with `--browser`, it opens the private setup page in your browser instead.

### onadit onboard

Does the same in the terminal, in 3 steps: add an archive, find something in it, connect a tool.

Some options start a longer setup instead, for Search by meaning, Capture, enrichment and feedback: `--advanced`, and the Voyage, Capture, enrichment, `--with-claude-hook` and feedback options in the table. The longer setup ignores `--query`, `--client` and `--source`, connects no tool, and imports ChatGPT exports only. Use `onadit import` for the others.

```sh
onadit onboard
onadit onboard --import-export ~/Downloads/export.zip --query "pricing" --client claude-code
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--import-export <path>` | Import this export (`.zip` or `.json`) without asking |
| `--no-import-export` | Skip the import step |
| `--source <name>` | The export's source, when it cannot be detected: `chatgpt_web`, `claude_web`, `gemini_web` or `grok_web`. 3-step setup only |
| `--query <words>` | What to look for after the import. 3-step setup only |
| `--client <name>` | The tool to connect: `claude-desktop`, `claude-code`, `codex` or `cursor`. 3-step setup only |
| `--yes` | Accept every default, for scripts |
| `--advanced` | Run the longer setup instead of the 3 steps: Voyage key, Capture, enrichment and feedback. On a Mac that already has a Voyage key, `--advanced` alone says so and stops |
| `--enable-capture` | Turn scheduled Capture on. Asks whether Claude Code or Codex reads your sessions. Needs a Voyage key: without one it is ignored |
| `--capture-worker <tool>` | `claude` or `codex`: answers that question, or switches the tool when Capture is already on. Required with `--yes` until a tool has been chosen |
| `--capture-level <level>` | `balanced` (the default) or `fast` |
| `--enable-grok-capture` | Add Grok CLI sessions to Capture, and turn Capture on. Needs a Voyage key |
| `--enable-cowork-capture` | Add Claude desktop agent sessions to Capture, and turn Capture on. Needs a Voyage key |
| `--no-codex-capture` | Skip the Capture check for this run |
| `--voyage-key <key>` | Save your own Voyage key for Search by meaning |
| `--no-voyage-key` | Finish with keyword search only |
| `--reconfigure-voyage` | Replace the saved Voyage key and nothing else |
| `--voyage-label <label>` | A display name for the Voyage project |
| `--enable-codex-enrichment` | Let Codex write richer summaries and weekly digests |
| `--enable-claude-enrichment` | Let Claude Code write richer summaries. Cannot be combined with the Codex option |
| `--with-claude-hook`, `--no-claude-hook` | In the longer setup: install, or skip, the Claude Code check before Onadit's tools. It does not add the session brief. The 3-step setup offers the hooks either way |
| `--skip-capture` | For tests. Skips the first Capture run after setup |
| `--enable-feedback-relay <url>`, `--no-feedback-relay`, `--invite <code>`, `--email <address>` | Feedback options, for people who were invited to send feedback. `--enable-feedback-relay` also needs the signing secret an invite gives. `--email` only saves your address on this Mac: nothing is sent without a relay |

## History

### onadit import

Imports an export from a chat app. See [Import](https://onadit.com/docs/import.md).

```sh
onadit import <file> [--source <source>] [--no-sniff] [--idempotency-key <key>]
onadit import ~/Downloads/chatgpt-export.zip
onadit import ~/Downloads/claude-export.zip --source claude_web
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--source <source>` | `chatgpt_web` (default), `claude_web`, `gemini_web` or `grok_web` |
| `--no-sniff` | Do not inspect the archive to check its source. Trust `--source` |
| `--idempotency-key <key>` | A key that makes a repeated import a no-op |

### onadit capture

Runs Capture once, now. See [Capture](https://onadit.com/docs/capture.md).

```sh
onadit capture [--dry-run] [--source <source>] [--claude-dir <path>] [--codex-dir <path>] [--cursor-dir <path>]
onadit capture recover-quarantine [--dry-run] [--chunk-bytes <bytes>]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Judge sessions but save nothing and change no state. Before a source's first real run, that means every session already on your Mac, each time you run it |
| `--source <source>` | Only 1 source: `claude_code`, `codex_cli`, `cursor_composer`, `claude_desktop_sessions` or `grok_cli` |
| `--claude-dir <path>` | Where Claude Code keeps its files |
| `--codex-dir <path>` | Where Codex keeps its files |
| `--cursor-dir <path>` | Cursor's application-support folder |
| `recover-quarantine` | Subcommand. Saves the Codex sessions that were too large for Capture: Codex summarises each one in pieces, and it is saved as 1 conversation. `--dry-run` shows what would be saved. `--chunk-bytes <bytes>` sets the piece size (default 524288) |

### onadit review

Manages the sessions Capture was unsure about.

```sh
onadit review list --min-confidence 0.6 --sort-by confidence --order desc
onadit review promote <id>
onadit review discard <id>
onadit review promote-many --source codex_cli --limit 20
onadit review discard-many --max-confidence 0.3
```

| Option | Applies to | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--source <source>` | list, promote-many, discard-many | Only 1 source |
| `--min-confidence <n>`, `--max-confidence <n>` | list, promote-many, discard-many | A confidence range, from 0 to 1 |
| `--topic <topic>` | list, promote-many, discard-many | Only 1 topic |
| `--queued-after <iso>`, `--queued-before <iso>` | list, promote-many, discard-many | A time range |
| `--search <text>` | list, promote-many, discard-many | Text in the summary, topics, source or project |
| `--sort-by <field>` | list, promote-many, discard-many | Sort by `queued` (the default), `confidence` or `source` |
| `--order <direction>` | list | `asc` or `desc`. By default the newest or the highest confidence comes first, and sources go from A to Z |
| `--page <n>`, `--per-page <n>` | list | Paging. 50 per page by default |
| `--ids <a,b,c>` | promote-many, discard-many | Act on these IDs |
| `--limit <n>` | promote-many, discard-many | Act on the first N matches only |

In 1.0.2, promote-many and discard-many accept `--order` but ignore it, so `--limit` always takes the newest matches first, or the highest confidence with `--sort-by confidence`, or A to Z with `--sort-by source`.

### onadit save

Saves 1 session or note. Agents normally do this through the `onadit_save` tool. See [Save from an agent](https://onadit.com/docs/save.md).

```sh
onadit save --source <source> --summary <text> [options]
onadit save --source claude_code --summary "Chose the queue over cron" --content-file session.txt
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--source <source>` | Required. `claude_code`, `gemini_cli` or `codex_cli` |
| `--summary <text>` | Required. A summary of the session |
| `--content <text>`, `--content-file <path>`, `--stdin` | The full transcript, given inline, from a file, or on standard input |
| `--domain <domain>` | 1 of `business`, `tech`, `personal`, `travel`, `health`, `finance` or `creative` |
| `--decisions <items>`, `--key-outputs <items>`, `--topics <items>` | Comma-separated lists |
| `--idempotency-key <key>` | A key that makes a repeated save a no-op |
| `--replace-idempotency-key <key>` | The key of an earlier save to replace |

### onadit backfill

Stages and imports a folder of web exports in 1 run.

```sh
onadit backfill --batch <path> --source <source> [options]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--batch <path>` | Required. The folder of exports |
| `--source <source>` | Required. `chatgpt_web`, `claude_web`, `gemini_web` or `grok_web` |
| `--dry-run` | Check the folder and write its manifest, then stop without importing |
| `--force-unstaged` | Import files even if the check flagged them as junk |
| `--limit <count>` | Stop after the first N files that are not yet imported |
| `--provider <provider>` | Use this tool to judge and summarise, for this run only. Supported: `codex-cli` |
| `--triage-provider <provider>` | The same, for judging only |
| `--extraction-provider <provider>` | The same, for summaries only |

### onadit bulk-ingest

Imports every supported file in a folder.

```sh
onadit bulk-ingest --source <source> --dir <path> [--idempotency-prefix <prefix>]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--source <source>` | Required. The source of every file in the folder, for example `chatgpt_web` |
| `--dir <path>` | Required. The folder |
| `--idempotency-prefix <prefix>` | A prefix for the keys that make a repeated run a no-op |

### onadit triage

Submits a folder of conversation files to be judged. Results land in `data/triage-results/`.

```sh
onadit triage --dir <path> [--idempotency-key <key>]
```

### onadit ingest

An older form of `onadit import`. Both options are required.

```sh
onadit ingest --source <source> --file <path> [--idempotency-key <key>]
```

### onadit cursor-probe

Lists the Cursor sessions Onadit could capture. It reads only and saves nothing.

```sh
onadit cursor-probe [--dir <path>] [--show-titles] [--show-provenance]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--dir <path>` | Cursor's application-support folder, if it is not the default |
| `--show-titles` | Show session titles. They are your own words and may reveal private content |
| `--show-provenance` | Show how each session would be recorded |

## Agents

### onadit mcp install

Adds Onadit to an MCP client's config file. See [Connect an agent](https://onadit.com/docs/connect.md).

```sh
onadit mcp install --client <id> [--dry-run] [--with-hooks | --no-hooks] [--new-names]
onadit mcp install --all [--dry-run]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--client <id>` | `claude-desktop`, `codex`, `claude-code` or `cursor` |
| `--all` | All 4 supported clients, whether or not they are installed. A missing config file is created |
| `--dry-run` | Print the change without writing it |
| `--with-hooks` | For Claude Code and Codex: also install the session hooks, without asking |
| `--no-hooks` | Do not offer the session hooks |
| `--new-names` | Move a connection made under the earlier `rift` names to the current ones. Rules written for the earlier tool names stop applying to it |

In a terminal, after connecting Claude Code or Codex, the command asks whether to turn on the session hooks described below.

### onadit hooks

Installs or removes the optional hooks for Claude Code or Codex. 1 asks the agent to call `onadit_context_pack` before an open-ended search, and 1 hands it a project brief when a session starts. Codex runs them only after you review them once with `/hooks` in Codex.

```sh
onadit hooks install --client <claude-code|codex> [--dry-run] [--no-session-brief]
onadit hooks remove --client <claude-code|codex>
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--client <id>` | Required. `claude-code` or `codex` |
| `--dry-run` | With `install`: print the outcome without writing it |
| `--no-session-brief` | With `install`: leave out the session-start brief |

`remove` takes Onadit's hooks back out, backs up the settings file first, and prints the backup ID.

## Maintenance

`reindex`, `reconcile`, `rebuild` and `compact` need a Voyage key, which Search by meaning sets. Without one, they stop with an "unavailable" error.

### onadit stats

Prints row counts per table. No options.

### onadit compact

Moves conversations older than 30 days to the archive table and writes 1 digest of them. It needs a Voyage key and Codex enrichment (`onadit onboard --enable-codex-enrichment`) or local generation. Without them it stops with "POST /compact unavailable". It runs only when you call it.

```sh
onadit compact [--dry-run] [--rollback] [--idempotency-key <key>]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Report what would move. Change nothing |
| `--rollback` | Undo the most recent compaction |
| `--idempotency-key <key>` | A key that makes a repeated run a no-op |

### onadit reindex

Rebuilds the search indexes from the raw files. `--scope` is required, and `--rebuild` works only with `--scope all`.

```sh
onadit reindex --scope <scope> [--idempotency-key <key>]
onadit reindex --scope all --rebuild [--idempotency-key <key>]
onadit reindex --scope conversations
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--scope <scope>` | Required. `all`, `conversations`, `documents` or `structured_docs` |
| `--rebuild` | Rebuild in full behind a shadow table, then swap it in. Only with `--scope all`. With another scope the command stops with "--rebuild requires --scope all" |
| `--idempotency-key <key>` | A key that makes a repeated run a no-op |

### onadit reconcile

Checks the index against the raw files and repairs gaps.

```sh
onadit reconcile [--idempotency-key <key>]
onadit reconcile --dedupe-conversations [--apply]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--dedupe-conversations` | Look for duplicate conversations and report them, in place of the normal checks |
| `--apply` | With `--dedupe-conversations`, delete the duplicates and their raw files. Without it, nothing is deleted |
| `--idempotency-key <key>` | A key that makes a repeated run a no-op |

### onadit rebuild

Rebuilds every table from the raw files.

```sh
onadit rebuild [--offline]
```

`--offline` runs without the engine, which must be stopped first. It needs `VOYAGE_API_KEY` set in your shell: it does not read `~/.rift.env`.

### onadit update

Terminal installs: installs the latest version, restarts the engine, and checks that the running engine reports the new version. Package installs: changes nothing and tells you to download the package. No options. See [Update](https://onadit.com/docs/install.md#update).

### onadit uninstall

```sh
onadit uninstall [--purge-data [-y | --yes]] [--notify]
```

See [Remove Onadit](https://onadit.com/docs/remove.md) for what each option does.

### onadit token issue

Issues a new access token, stores it in the Keychain, tells the engine, and prints it. No options.

### onadit menubar install

Installs or refreshes the menu-bar plugin. The item shows once SwiftBar is installed.

```sh
onadit menubar install [--plugin-dir <path>] [--symlink] [--yes]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--plugin-dir <path>` | SwiftBar's plugin folder, if it is not the default |
| `--symlink` | Link to the packaged files instead of copying them. For development checkouts |
| `--yes` | Accepted for install scripts. The command never asks anything |

### onadit feedback

Stores a note in a local file. It is sent to us only if you were invited to send feedback and accepted.

```sh
onadit feedback [--kind <kind>] [--with-status] <note>
onadit feedback --history
onadit feedback setup [--invite <code>]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--kind <kind>` | Tag the note: `worked`, `broke`, `surprised` or `idea` |
| `--with-status` | Attach a status snapshot, with paths and content removed |
| `--history` | Print the notes stored on this Mac |
| `setup --invite <code>` | Turn sending on, with the invite code you were given |

## Internal commands and options

These exist in the command line but are not meant for everyday use. They are listed so that nothing you see in `--help` is unexplained.

| Command or option | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `onadit chunk-backfill [--dry-run] [--limit <n>] [--throttle-ms <ms>] [--allow-uncertified-copy]` | For Onadit's maintainers. Re-splits old conversations into passages, with the engine stopped |
| `onadit uninstall --result-file <path>` | Hidden. Lets Onadit.app read the outcome of a removal |
| `onadit setup --app-session` | Hidden. Hands Onadit.app a setup session |
| `onadit mcp refresh [--leaving <dir>] [--dry-run]` | Hidden. The installers run it after an upgrade to point existing connections and hooks at the new build. It creates none |
| `onadit onboard --relay-secret <secret>`, `--allow-unsigned-feedback-relay` | Hidden. For the feedback relay |


---
title: Configuration
url: https://onadit.com/docs/configuration
summary: Onadit reads 1 JSON file when the engine starts. This page lists every key, its type and its default, and the environment variables Onadit reads.
last_updated: 2026-10-22
---

# Configuration

Onadit reads 1 JSON file when the engine starts. This page lists every key, its type and its default, and the environment variables Onadit reads.

## The file

| | |
|---|---|
| Location | `~/Library/Application Support/Rift/data/config.json` |
| Override | `--config <path>` on any command, or the `RIFT_CONFIG` environment variable, for the command line. The engine reads the path its launch agent gives it |
| Format | JSON |
| Read | Once, when the engine starts. Restart the engine after a change. |
| Unknown keys | Rejected. A file with a key this version does not know fails to load. |

Restart the engine with:

```sh
launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.getrift.daemon
```

## The default file

This is what the installer writes. Capture and enrichment are off.

```json config.json
{
  "sources": [
    { "path": "~/Library/Application Support/Rift/data/inbox", "extraction": "cloud", "mode": "watch", "scope": "project" }
  ],
  "embedding": { "provider": "voyage", "model": "voyage-3-lite" },
  "data_paths": {
    "data_dir": "~/Library/Application Support/Rift/data",
    "jobs_dir": "~/Library/Application Support/Rift/jobs"
  },
  "rate_limit": { "window_ms": 60000, "max_requests": 100 },
  "capture": { "enabled": false, "interval_seconds": 3600, "sources": ["claude_code", "codex_cli"] },
  "enrichment": { "ai_metadata": false }
}
```

The real file holds absolute paths. They are shortened to `~` here.

## Keys

### sources

Folders whose documents Onadit indexes. At least 1 is required. The default is the inbox. With no embedding key, `cloud` folders are not indexed.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sources[].path` | string | required | An absolute folder path |
| `sources[].extraction` | `"cloud"` or `"local"` | required | Where the text is embedded: with Voyage, or on your Mac with Ollama's `nomic-embed-text` at `localhost:11434`. With a `local` source, the engine does not start if Ollama cannot be reached |
| `sources[].mode` | `"watch"` or `"scheduled_scan"` | required | Watch the folder for changes, or scan it on a schedule. A schedule needs `cron.cron_enabled` |
| `sources[].scope` | `"client"`, `"project"` or `"document"` | required | How results from this folder are grouped |
| `sources[].client_name` | string | none | Required when `scope` is `"client"` |
| `sources[].exclude` | string array | none | Relative paths inside the folder to skip |
| `scan.interval_seconds` | integer | `604800` | How often scheduled sources are scanned. The default is 7 days |
| `cron.cron_enabled` | boolean | `false` | Must be `true` for `scheduled_scan` sources to be scanned at all |

### capture

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capture.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns scheduled Capture on |
| `capture.interval_seconds` | integer | `3600` | Seconds between runs |
| `capture.sources` | string array | `["claude_code", "codex_cli"]` | Any of `claude_code`, `codex_cli`, `cursor_composer`, `claude_desktop_sessions`, `grok_cli` |
| `capture.triage.provider` | `"codex_cli"` or `"claude_code"` | `"codex_cli"` | Which of your tools judges and summarises sessions. Asked when you turn Capture on. If the key is missing, Codex is used |
| `capture.triage.level` | `"balanced"` or `"fast"` | `"balanced"` | The model level: Claude `sonnet` or `haiku`, or the matching Codex model. With Codex, it sets the model of every Codex call: summaries, digests and recovery too. See [Capture](https://onadit.com/docs/capture.md#claude-code-or-codex-and-the-model) |
| `capture.codex_cli.max_session_bytes` | integer | 8 MB | Codex sessions above this size skip normal judging. With Codex as Capture's worker, Onadit then summarises them with Codex in 512 KB pieces |
| `capture.cursor.max_session_bytes` | integer | 4 MB | The same, for Cursor sessions |
| `codex_cli.model` | string | none | An exact Codex model, instead of the one picked for the level |

### embedding and enrichment

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `embedding.provider` | `"voyage"` | required | The embedding provider for Search by meaning |
| `embedding.model` | string | `"voyage-3-lite"` | The embedding model. A key provided by Onadit sets this to `voyage-4-lite` |
| `embedding.base_url` | URL | Voyage's API | Another endpoint for the same API |
| `embedding.output_dimension` | integer | none | The vector size to request. The tables hold 512-dimension vectors, so a model that offers several sizes needs `512` |
| `voyage.project_label` | string | none | A display name for the Voyage project |
| `enrichment.ai_metadata` | boolean | `false` | Let one of your tools write richer summaries on import |
| `enrichment.metadata.provider` | `"codex_cli"` or `"claude_code"` | `"codex_cli"` | Which tool writes them |
| `local_generation.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Use a local Ollama model for summaries and digests |
| `local_generation.runtime` | `"ollama"` | none | Required when enabled |
| `local_generation.mode` | `"strict_local_only"` | `"strict_local_only"` | The only mode. Summaries go only to `local_generation.base_url`, which is your Mac unless you change it |
| `local_generation.base_url` | URL | `"http://localhost:11434"` | Where Ollama listens, for summaries and digests. Local embeddings always use `localhost:11434` |
| `local_generation.metadata_model` | string | none | Required when enabled |
| `local_generation.digest_model` | string | none | Required when enabled |

### server and limits

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `server.port` | integer | `3577` | The engine's port. The installer and `onadit update` assume 3577 |
| `server.host` | `"127.0.0.1"` | `"127.0.0.1"` | Cannot be changed. The engine never listens on the network |
| `rate_limit.window_ms` | integer | required | The length of the rate-limit window |
| `rate_limit.max_requests` | integer | required | Requests allowed per window |
| `request_limits.json_body_limit_bytes` | integer | `10485760` | Largest JSON request, 10 MB |
| `request_limits.multipart_limit_bytes` | integer | `104857600` | Largest upload, 100 MB |
| `request_limits.read_timeout_ms` | integer | `30000` | Time limit for receiving a request, on every route |

### storage and schedules

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data_paths.data_dir` | string | `"data"` | Where the archive lives. A relative path is resolved from the config file's folder |
| `data_paths.jobs_dir` | string | `"jobs"` | Where the job queue lives |
| `compaction.age_threshold_days` | integer | `30` | Conversations older than this move to the cold table |

### Reserved and internal keys

The file accepts these keys, but you should not need them. They are listed so the reference is complete.

| Key | Type | Default | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `compaction.schedule` | cron string | `"0 2 * * 0"` | Reserved. Nothing reads it in this version. Compaction runs when you call `onadit compact` |
| `request_limits.mutation_timeout_ms` | integer | `120000` | Reserved. Nothing reads it in this version |
| `openai.max_cost_per_batch_usd` | number | `5` | Reserved. It only counts spending on OpenAI's API, which this version never calls |
| `openai.max_parallel_requests` | integer | `4` | Internal. The most Codex calls an `onadit triage` job runs at once |
| `auth.test_token` | string | none | Internal. For automated tests |

## Your Voyage key

If you use your own Voyage key for Search by meaning, it is kept in `~/.rift.env`, readable by you only, as `VOYAGE_API_KEY`. The engine loads that file when it starts. It reads 3 names from it and ignores the rest: `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Only the first is needed for anything on this page. Replace the key with:

```sh
onadit onboard --reconfigure-voyage
```

## Environment variables

The engine is started by launchd, so it does not see what you export in your shell. To set a variable for the engine, add it to `EnvironmentVariables` in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.getrift.daemon.plist`. The package installer keeps those entries when you update. A variable read by the command line goes in your shell, and one read by a hook goes in the environment of the tool that runs it.

| Variable | Read by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `RIFT_CONFIG` | Command line | The config file the command line uses by default |
| `VOYAGE_API_KEY` | Engine, and `onadit rebuild --offline` | The embedding key. Without it, search is keyword only |
| `RIFT_CLAUDE_CLI_PATH` | Engine | The `claude` binary to use when Claude Code judges or summarises sessions |
| `CODEX_HOME` | Engine | Codex's home folder |
| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | Engine | Claude Code's config folder |
| `RIFT_SWIFTBAR_PLUGIN_DIR` | `onadit menubar` | SwiftBar's plugin folder, if it is not the default |
| `RIFT_POLICY_DISABLED` | The hook, inside Claude Code or Codex | `1` turns the check before Onadit's tools into a no-op |
| `RIFT_DISABLE_AI_METADATA` | Engine | `1` forces plain summaries, with no AI tool involved |
| `RIFT_DISABLE_WATCHERS` | Engine | `1` stops the engine from watching folders |

### Switches for features that are off by default

The engine reads all of these.

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `RIFT_CHUNKING` | `1` splits long conversations into passages when they are indexed |
| `RIFT_INDEX_CARDS` | `1` lets short cards for report files into search results |
| `RIFT_FEEDBACK_RANKING` | `1` lets recorded outcomes influence ranking |
| `RIFT_CONV_DEDUP` | `0` turns off the merging of duplicate conversations in results. On by default |
| `RIFT_CANONICAL_FILES` | `0` stops project tracker files from being read into context packs. On by default |
| `RIFT_RECEIPT` | `0` removes the 1-line note about what Onadit recalled from responses. On by default |

### Internal and development variables

You should not need these. Variables used only by the tests of the app and the installers are left out.

| Variable | Used by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `RIFT_LOCATOR_BOOST`, `RIFT_LOCATOR_DEMOTE_EXCEPTION` | Engine | Ranking experiments |
| `RIFT_CURSOR_CAPTURE`, `RIFT_CURSOR_SHOW_TITLES` | Engine | One-off Cursor discovery, and showing Cursor session titles |
| `CURSOR_CAPTURE_PERSIST` | Engine | `1` lets a one-off Cursor capture save what it finds. Adding `cursor_composer` to `capture.sources` is the normal way |
| `RIFT_KEY_RELAY_URL` | Engine | Another address for the key service |
| `RIFT_COMMIT` | Engine | The commit reported in build information |
| `RIFT_TRACE_WORKER`, `RIFT_TRACE_WORKER_PATH` | Engine | Tracing of worker processes |
| `NODE_ENV` | Engine | Set to `production` by the launch agent |
| `RIFT_SKIP_POSTINSTALL_MENUBAR`, `RIFT_POSTINSTALL_MENUBAR`, `RIFT_SKIP_POSTINSTALL_REFRESH` | npm install | Whether the menu-bar and connection-refresh steps run after an npm install |
| `RIFT_PACKAGE_SPEC`, `RIFT_SKIP_BOOTSTRAP`, `RIFT_INSTALL_DEBUG`, `RIFT_INSTALL_RESOLVE_ONLY`, `RIFT_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_S`, `RIFT_BOOTOUT_PORT_FREE_DECISECONDS` | Terminal installer | Which package to install, debugging, and timeouts |
| `RIFT_BASE_URL`, `RIFT_LOG_DIR`, `RIFT_CODEX_BIN`, `RIFT_BIN`, `RIFT_JS` | Menu-bar item | Where the engine, the logs, Codex and the command line are |
| `RIFT_APP_HOME`, `RIFT_APP_NODE`, `RIFT_APP_CLI`, `RIFT_APP_CONFIG`, `RIFT_APP_LAUNCHD_LABEL` | Onadit.app | Development and tests only |


---
title: Troubleshooting
url: https://onadit.com/docs/troubleshooting
summary: Start with onadit doctor. It names what is wrong and gives 1 action. This page lists every state it can report and every line onadit status prints.
last_updated: 2026-10-22
---

# Troubleshooting

Start with onadit doctor. It names what is wrong and gives 1 action. This page lists every state it can report and every line onadit status prints.

## Start here

```sh
onadit doctor
```

```text When all is well
Onadit is working. Nothing needs attention.
```

Most Macs also see a warning or 2, such as a supported tool that is not connected or SwiftBar that is not installed. Those do not stop Onadit from working.

If the shell answers `command not found: onadit`, the command is not on your `PATH`. A package install puts it at `~/.rift/bin/onadit`. Use that full path, or [add the folder to your PATH](https://onadit.com/docs/install.md#use-the-command-line).

`onadit doctor` only reads. It exits with code 1 when something is broken. To hand the problem to an agent, run `onadit doctor --copy-prompt`. It builds a prompt with private details removed and copies it.

## The engine does not answer

| What you see | Cause | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| "Onadit isn't set up on this Mac yet" | Setup has not run here: there is no config file, or no access token yet | `onadit onboard` |
| "Onadit's daemon rejected this command's token" | The token is out of date, or the login Keychain is locked, which is common over SSH | `onadit token issue` |
| "Onadit's background engine is not responding" | The engine is not running | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.getrift.daemon` |
| "Login Keychain is locked" | Common over SSH | `security unlock-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db` |
| The package fails to install, or the terminal installer says port 3577 is in use | Another program holds the port. The package writes the reason to `/var/log/install.log` | Stop that program, then install again |

Engine logs are in `~/Library/Logs/Rift/` on a package install, and in `~/Library/Application Support/Rift/logs/` on a terminal install.

## What doctor can report

Doctor checks these in order and leads with the first one that is broken. Errors from before the engine last started are ignored.

| State | Level | Means | Do this |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voyage_key_missing` | Broken | Capture is on and there is no embedding key | Turn Search by meaning on in the app's Privacy settings, or `onadit onboard --reconfigure-voyage` |
| `semantic_search_off` | Warning | No embedding key. Keyword search works | The same, if you want search by meaning |
| `codex_auth_expired` | Broken | Codex is signed out | `codex login` |
| `codex_preflight_failed` | Broken | Codex could not run. See the table below | Depends on the cause |
| `claude_auth_expired` | Broken | Claude Code is signed out | Run `claude` and sign in |
| `claude_preflight_failed` | Broken | Claude Code could not run. See the table below | Depends on the cause |
| `voyage_embed_errors` | Broken | An embedding request failed | `onadit status`, then `onadit onboard --reconfigure-voyage` if it names the key |
| `index_write_errors` | Broken | A write to the index failed | `onadit status`, then `onadit reindex` |
| `capture_failed` | Broken | The last Capture run had errors | Nothing. Onadit retries |
| `capture_daemon_stale` | Warning | A scheduled run failed, but a later manual run worked | Nothing |
| `inbox_import_errors` | Warning | An export dropped in the inbox could not be read | Export again and drop the new file |
| `mcp_not_installed` | Warning | 1 of the 4 supported tools has no Onadit entry. It is listed even if that tool is not installed | `onadit mcp install --client=<name>`, or nothing if you do not use that tool |
| `earlier_names_left` | Warning | A rule file of yours still names the earlier `rift_` tools, so those lines no longer match | In the file it names, replace `rift_` with `onadit_` and `mcp__rift__` with `mcp__onadit__` |
| `menu_bar_unavailable` | Warning | SwiftBar is not installed | Install SwiftBar, then `onadit menubar install` |
| `menu_bar_broken` | Warning | The menu-bar plugin is damaged | `onadit menubar install` |
| `capture_quarantined` | Warning | Some sessions were too large and ran out of retries | `onadit doctor repair capture-large-sessions` |
| `capture_repairing` | Warning | Large sessions are being saved in the background | Nothing |
| `update_available` | Warning | A newer version is out | See [Update](https://onadit.com/docs/install.md#update) |

## When Capture cannot use Codex

Capture runs a short check before each run. If it fails, `onadit status` shows why.

| Cause | Message | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| `auth` | "Codex login appears to have expired." | `codex login` |
| `model` | "Codex rejected the model …" | Set `codex_cli.model` in the config to a model your plan offers |
| `cli_incompatible` | "Codex CLI is too old for capture" | Upgrade Codex |
| `binary` | "Codex CLI could not be found or started" | Check that it is installed and on the `PATH` |
| `rate_limit` | "Codex hit a rate/usage limit or is out of credits" | Wait, or check your plan |
| `capacity` | "OpenAI's Codex models were at capacity" | Nothing. Onadit uses another model, and retries on its next pass |
| `timeout`, `backend`, `unknown` | A timeout or a network problem | Nothing. Onadit retries |

These are problems with the Codex install or its sign-in. Onadit does not hold a Codex or OpenAI key.

## When Capture cannot use Claude Code

| Cause | Do this |
|---|---|
| `missing` | Install Claude Code, or set `RIFT_CLAUDE_CLI_PATH` |
| `incompatible` | Upgrade Claude Code |
| `wrapper` | A wrapper script is in the way. Set `RIFT_CLAUDE_CLI_PATH` to the real binary |
| `auth` | Run `claude` and sign in |
| `rate_limit` | Wait |
| `network` | Check your connection |
| `timeout`, `unknown` | Nothing. Onadit retries |

## What onadit status prints

| Line | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| Header | The version, whether the engine is running and for how long, and the port. A tick after the port means an embedding key is set. A cross means Capture is on with no embedding key |
| `Voyage:` | The embedding key is valid, and when it was last used. Replaced by `Search:` when there is no key |
| `Search:` | `keyword on · semantic off` when there is no key |
| `Index:` | When the index was last written, and the last error if there was one |
| `Inbox:` | Whether an export was dropped in `data/inbox/`, and how many are pending |
| `Memory:` | How many conversations and documents Onadit holds, digests when AI enrichment writes them, and why a count is 0 |
| `Codex CLI:` or `Claude Code:` | Whether the tool Capture uses is signed in and working |
| `Model:` | When Capture is on: the model that reads sessions, and its level |
| `Codex model:` | Only after Onadit switched Codex to another model, and when |
| `Capture:` | Starts with `off`, `on`, `working` or `failed`. Then the last run: how many sessions were saved or sent to review, `nothing new` if there were none, and when the next run is due |
| `Automatic:` | Only when a manual run worked but the last scheduled run failed |
| `Cursor:`, `Cowork:`, `Grok CLI:` | Whether each opt-in source is on, and how to turn it on |
| `App chats:` | Chat apps found on this Mac whose chats need an export |
| `MCP:` | Which tools are connected. A cross comes with the command that fixes it |
| `Menu bar:` | Only shown when the menu-bar item is missing or broken |
| `Feedback:` | Whether you opted in to sending feedback |
| `Update:` | Only shown when a newer version is out |
| `First recall:` | Whether an AI tool has had a complete answer with results from Onadit yet |
| `Heads up:` | Only when the command line is older than your config |
| `Setup:`, `Config:` | Only before setup is finished: what is left to do |
| `Next:` | 1 action, or "nothing broken" |

The reasons a `Memory:` count can be 0: for digests, `none yet`, `digest worker unavailable` or `unknown`. For documents, `no sources`, `source missing`, `source empty`, `Voyage key missing`, `backfill needed` or `unknown`.

## Other messages

| Message | Do this |
|---|---|
| "Authentication failed. Run: onadit token issue" | Run it |
| "Cannot connect to daemon" | Restart the engine with the `launchctl kickstart` command above |
| "Config not found" | `onadit onboard`, or point `RIFT_CONFIG` at the file |
| "Config invalid" | Fix the key it names. Unknown keys are rejected |
| "has keys this CLI does not recognize" | The config was written by a newer version. Update Onadit |
| "Rate limited. Retry later." | Wait a minute |
| "Another exclusive operation is running" | A rebuild or reindex is in progress. Wait for it |

## Common fixes

- The menu-bar icon is missing: open SwiftBar, then run `onadit menubar install`
- A hook gets in the way: `onadit hooks remove --client claude-code` (or `codex`) removes it, and `RIFT_POLICY_DISABLED=1` silences only the check before Onadit's tools
- Search by meaning stopped working: `onadit onboard --reconfigure-voyage` replaces the key
- An agent does not use Onadit: check the `MCP:` line in `onadit status`, then add [the line to your rule file](https://onadit.com/docs/instructions.md)


---
title: Limits
url: https://onadit.com/docs/limits
summary: What Onadit does not do today, stated plainly.
last_updated: 2026-10-22
---

# Limits

What Onadit does not do today, stated plainly.

## Platform

- Mac only, with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later (12.3 or later for the terminal install), and there is no Intel, Windows or Linux build

## History

- Capture reads Claude Code and Codex sessions, plus the opt-in sources listed in [Capture](https://onadit.com/docs/capture.md)
- Capture starts on the day you turn it on, so sessions that existed before are not imported unless you resume them (Grok CLI is the exception: turning it on captures its old sessions too)
- Capture needs Search by meaning to be on, since the capture loop does not start without an embedding key
- An imported conversation is dated by its import, not by when it took place
- Chat apps come in through an export file that you request from the provider, since Onadit cannot read ordinary chats in the ChatGPT or Claude desktop apps

## Agents

- Only MCP clients can search Onadit: importing a ChatGPT export puts those chats in Onadit, but it does not let the ChatGPT app search Onadit
- An agent decides when to call Onadit, and without [a line in your rule file](https://onadit.com/docs/instructions.md) it may not

## Privacy

- A passage an agent recalls becomes part of its conversation, so it reaches that agent's provider
- The archive is not walled off by project: `cwd` narrows documents and puts the current project's conversations first in a context pack, but conversations from other projects can still come back, and `onadit_search` does not filter conversations by `cwd`
- Capture summarises sessions through your own Claude Code or Codex, so session text goes to that provider and uses some of your plan (we have not published how much)
- Search by meaning, when on, sends passages and questions to Voyage's models, hosted by MongoDB Atlas with the key Onadit provides, while keyword search sends nothing

## Evidence

- We have no measured figure for tokens saved or for answer quality
- The speed figures come from 16 fixed tasks on 1 Mac (the conditions are in [Performance](https://onadit.com/docs/performance.md))
